feedback: I reviewed the iteration 2 candidate: base_speed 1.2, kp 3.5, kd 0.6, ki 0, line_loss last_direction, with geometry and sensor weights unchanged from iteration 1. It has not raced, so I state no outcome for it. The design is valid: all values are inside the contract ranges and the sensor layout is unchanged. The change is a single variable, base_speed 1.3 to 1.2, which follows the requested change from iteration 1. The evidence behind it is iteration 1 (score 556.7). The oval finished in 100% of trials at mean 2.03 s, so it has time margin. On the s-bend, 11 of 20 trials ended off track, and the slalom ended off track in all 20 trials at progress 0.30 with max_error 0.064 and 1.15 line-loss events per run. Lowering speed should reduce centripetal and slip error on the tight arcs and cut line loss. Approve this now. It is a minimal, well-isolated test, and the race will show whether speed was the limiting factor. Once the race reports back, read these numbers together. If the oval completion_time stays under about 2.5 s and the slalom or s-bend progress rises above the iteration 1 values (0.30 slalom, 0.88 s-bend), keep base_speed at 1.2 and test kp 3.8 with kd 0.7 to see whether steering authority is now the limit. If the oval completion_time rises above about 2.5 s, or the average speed looks too low for the 3.0 s limit, return to base_speed 1.3 and change the controller instead. If the slalom still ends off track with max_error above 0.06 and line_loss_events near 1.0, the next test is line_loss 'search_left' or 'search_right' only if the last-direction signal shows the robot leaving the tape on one side. Keep ki at 0 unless a one-sided offset appears.
